problems.title: A set encoded by its distance function
problems.statement_md:
For a nonempty set $E\subset\mathbb R^d$, define $d_E(x)=\inf_{y\in E}|x-y|$. Prove that $d_E$ is 1-Lipschitz, $d_E=d_{\overline E}$, and $\{d_E=0\}=\overline E$. For nonempty closed sets $E,F$, prove
$$E\subset F\iff d_E\geq d_F,\qquad d_{E\cup F}=\min(d_E,d_F).$$
Explain why distance functions cannot distinguish an open ball from its closure.
problems.hint_md: Apply the triangle inequality before taking the infimum. Test an inequality of distance functions on their zero sets.

problems.title: Hausdorff distance is uniform distance between distance functions
problems.statement_md:
For nonempty compact $K,L\subset\mathbb R^d$, define
$$d_H(K,L)=\max\{\max_{x\in K}d_L(x),\max_{y\in L}d_K(y)\}.$$
Prove
$$d_H(K,L)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}|d_K(x)-d_L(x)|=\max_{x\in K\cup L}|d_K(x)-d_L(x)|.$$
Deduce the triangle inequality and
$$d_H(K,L)\leq\varepsilon\iff K\subset L+\varepsilon B,\ L\subset K+\varepsilon B$$
for $\varepsilon\geq0$, where $B$ is the closed unit ball. No convexity is assumed.
problems.hint_md: Use a nearest point in one set to compare the two distances at an arbitrary point. On either set, one distance is zero.

problems.title: Support functions as a geometry calculator
problems.statement_md: For a nonempty compact convex set $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, put $h_K(u)=\max_{x\in K}x\cdot u$. Compute the support functions of a ball $B(c,r)$, a segment $[a,b]$, and $\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}$. Prove $h_{K+L}=h_K+h_L$ and $h_{\operatorname{conv}(K\cup L)}=\max(h_K,h_L)$. Finally prove the half-space representation $K=\bigcap_{|u|=1}\{x:x\cdot u\leq h_K(u)\}$, and deduce $K\subset L\iff h_K\leq h_L$. You may use separation of a point from a closed convex set.
problems.hint_md: A linear functional cannot exceed its largest value on the vertices of a convex combination. In a Minkowski sum, maximize over the two summands independently.

sources.locator: §1.7; outline Exercises 1.1, 1.4(i), 1.5

problems.title: Hausdorff distance and support functions
problems.statement_md:
For nonempty compact convex sets $K,L\subset\mathbb R^d$, prove the three-way identity
$$d_H(K,L)=\|h_K-h_L\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb S^{d-1})}=\|d_K-d_L\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^d)}.$$
Deduce that widths in any direction change by at most $2d_H(K,L)$. Explain why convexity is essential for the support-function equality by comparing the unit circle with the closed unit disk. You may use separation of a point from a closed convex set.
problems.hint_md: Express Hausdorff distance through two parallel-neighborhood inclusions, then translate inclusion into support inequalities. Support functions see only a set’s convex hull.

problems.title: Distance to a convex body from its support function
problems.statement_md:
Let $K$ be nonempty, compact and convex. Prove
$$d_K(x)=\max\left\{0,\max_{u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}}(x\cdot u-h_K(u))\right\}.$$
If $K$ has nonempty interior, prove that the maximum without the outer zero equals the signed distance
$$s_K(x)=\begin{cases}d_K(x),&x\notin K,\\-\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial K),&x\in K.\end{cases}$$
The sign convention is negative inside.
problems.hint_md: Outside $K$, use the supporting plane through a nearest point. Inside $K$, find the largest ball centered at $x$ lying in $K$.

sources.locator: Distance-function framework, §2.2.6.1, pp. 43–44; convex support-function companion; English edition (2018), printed pages

problems.title: Recognizing a Hausdorff limit by convergent points
problems.statement_md:
Suppose nonempty compact sets $K_n,K$ all lie in one fixed compact set $Q\subset\mathbb R^d$. Prove that $d_H(K_n,K)\to0$ is equivalent to both conditions:

1. Whenever $n_j\to\infty$, $x_j\in K_{n_j}$ and $x_j\to x$, then $x\in K$.
2. Every $x\in K$ admits points $x_n\in K_n$ with $x_n\to x$.

Deduce that inclusion and convexity are preserved under compact-set Hausdorff convergence.
problems.hint_md: If either directed distance stays positive, choose points witnessing that gap and use compactness of $Q$.

sources.locator: §2.2.3.2, properties (3)–(4), pp. 32–33; English edition (2018), printed pages

problems.title: Convex hull and union are stable; intersection need not be
problems.statement_md:
For nonempty compact sets, prove
$$d_H(K_1\cup K_2,L_1\cup L_2)\leq\max_i d_H(K_i,L_i),$$
$$d_H(\operatorname{conv}K,\operatorname{conv}L)\leq d_H(K,L).$$
You may use Carathéodory’s theorem to establish compactness of the convex hulls. Give compact convex $K_n,L_n$ with nonempty intersections such that $K_n\to K$, $L_n\to L$, but $K_n\cap L_n$ does not tend to $K\cap L$.
problems.hint_md: Approximate the points in a convex combination by points in the other set with the same coefficients. For failure of intersection, tilt one segment toward another.

sources.locator: Exercise 2.5, p. 63; compact-set Hausdorff properties in §2.2.3.2; English edition (2018), printed pages

problems.title: Nested compact sets converge to the expected limit
problems.statement_md: Prove that a decreasing sequence of nonempty compact sets $K_n$ converges in Hausdorff distance to $\bigcap_nK_n$. Prove that an increasing sequence of nonempty compact sets confined to a fixed compact set converges to $\overline{\bigcup_nK_n}$. Explain why confinement matters in the increasing case.
problems.hint_md: Use the convergent-points criterion. For an increasing family, once a point is well approximated it remains well approximated.

sources.locator: §2.2.3.2, compact-set properties (1)–(2), p. 32; English edition (2018), printed pages

problems.title: Compactness of sets from Arzelà–Ascoli
problems.statement_md: Let $Q\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact. Prove that every sequence of nonempty compact subsets $K_n\subset Q$ has a Hausdorff-convergent subsequence with nonempty compact limit in $Q$. Use Arzelà–Ascoli on the distance functions on $Q$; in particular, justify why a uniform limit of these functions is still a distance function.
problems.hint_md: Let the candidate limit set be the zero set of the limiting function. Take limits of nearest points to recover the function.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.2.25 and Proposition 2.2.27, pp. 42–44; English edition (2018), printed pages

problems.title: Open domains: measure distance between the complements
problems.statement_md:
For bounded open sets $\Omega,\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$, choose a closed ball $Q$ containing both and define
$$d_H^c(\Omega,\Lambda)=d_H(Q\setminus\Omega,Q\setminus\Lambda).$$
Set $q_\Omega(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathbb R^d\setminus\Omega)$. Prove
$$d_H^c(\Omega,\Lambda)=\|q_\Omega-q_\Lambda\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^d)},$$
so the definition is independent of $Q$. Show that $d_H^c(\varnothing,\Omega)$ is the supremal radius of balls contained in $\Omega$. Compute this distance between the open unit ball $U$ and the punctured ball $U\setminus\{0\}$, whose closures coincide.
problems.hint_md: Inside the open set, a nearest complement point lies on its boundary; outside it the distance is zero.

sources.locator: Definitions 2.2.8–2.2.10, pp. 30–31; Lemma 2.2.12 and Remarks 2.2.11–2.2.14, pp. 31–32; English edition (2018), printed pages

problems.title: Compact subsets survive domain convergence
problems.statement_md:
Suppose bounded open sets $\Omega_n,\Omega$ lie in one fixed ball and $d_H^c(\Omega_n,\Omega)\to0$. Show that every compact $F\subset\Omega$ eventually lies in $\Omega_n$. Deduce
$$|\Omega\setminus\Omega_n|\to0,\qquad |\Omega|\leq\liminf_n|\Omega_n|.$$
Give the same persistence conclusion for the support of a continuous function compactly supported in $\Omega$.
problems.hint_md: The clearance $q_\Omega$ has a positive minimum on $F$. Then use pointwise eventual membership inside $\Omega$.

problems.title: One grid, three different notions of convergence
problems.statement_md:
In $[0,1]$, let $G_n=\{j/n:0\leq j\leq n\}$ and $\Omega_n=(0,1)\setminus G_n$. Prove
$$d_H(G_n,[0,1])=\frac1{2n},\qquad d_H^c(\Omega_n,\varnothing)=\frac1{2n}.$$
Compare the Lebesgue measures of the limits with those of the approximating sets. Explain why all $\overline{\Omega_n}=[0,1]$ and all $1_{\Omega_n}=1_{(0,1)}$ almost everywhere, while $\Omega_n$ converges to the empty set in complementary Hausdorff distance.
problems.hint_md: The farthest point from the grid is the midpoint of a grid interval. Each open component has inradius $1/(2n)$.

problems.title: Compact convergence can have two different open limits
problems.statement_md: Use the following definition: $\Omega_n$ converges compactly to open $\Omega$ if every compact $F\subset\Omega$ eventually lies in $\Omega_n$, and every compact $G\subset\mathbb R^d\setminus\overline\Omega$ eventually lies in $\mathbb R^d\setminus\overline{\Omega_n}$. Show that the open balls $\Omega_n=\{x:|x|<1+1/n\}$ converge compactly both to the open unit ball $U$ and to $U\setminus\{0\}$. Then prove: if $\Omega_n$ converges compactly to $\Omega$ and $|\partial\Omega|=0$, its indicators converge in $L^p_{\rm loc}$ for every finite $p\geq1$.
problems.hint_md: The two candidate limits have the same closure. Away from the boundary, singleton compact sets decide eventual membership.

sources.locator: Definition 2.2.21, p. 38; §2.2.5, first counterexample, p. 39; Exercise 2.7, p. 63; English edition (2018), printed pages

problems.title: Symmetric difference and convergence of indicators
problems.statement_md:
Let measurable $E,F$ lie in a fixed bounded measurable set $Q$. Prove for $1\leq p<\infty$ that
$$\|1_E-1_F\|_{L^p}^p=|E\mathbin\triangle F|.$$
Show that $|E\triangle F|$ is a metric on sets modulo equality almost everywhere, whereas the $L^\infty$ distance is either zero or one. Finally, if $1_{E_n}$ converges weak-* in $L^\infty(Q)$ to $1_E$, prove convergence in every finite $L^p(Q)$ and the existence of an almost-everywhere convergent subsequence. Do not assume almost-everywhere convergence of the whole sequence.
problems.hint_md: The absolute indicator difference is itself an indicator. For the weak-* assertion, test against $1$ and $1_E$.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.2.1 and Remarks 2.2.4–2.2.5, pp. 27–29; Exercise 2.10(1)–(2), p. 64; English edition (2018), printed pages

problems.title: Fine alternating intervals converge to a density, not a set
problems.statement_md: Let $E_n=\bigcup_{j=0}^{n-1}(j/n,(j+1/2)/n)\subset(0,1)$. Prove $1_{E_n}\rightharpoonup^*1/2$ in $L^\infty(0,1)$, but that there is no strong $L^p$ limit for any finite $p\geq1$. Determine the complementary Hausdorff limit of $E_n$. You may use density of continuous functions in $L^1(0,1)$.
problems.hint_md: On each cell of length $1/n$, compare a continuous test function with its value at the cell’s left endpoint.

sources.locator: Exercise 2.1, p. 61; Proposition 2.2.28, p. 45 (uniform-cell variant); English edition (2018), printed pages

problems.title: Convexity restores volume convergence
problems.statement_md:
Let compact convex $K_n$ converge in Hausdorff distance to a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interior. After translating, suppose $rB\subset K$ for some $r>0$. With $\delta_n=d_H(K_n,K)<r$, prove
$$(1-\delta_n/r)K\subset K_n\subset(1+\delta_n/r)K.$$
Deduce $|K_n\triangle K|\to0$, volume convergence, and eventual inclusion of every compact subset of $\operatorname{int}K$ in $\operatorname{int}K_n$.
problems.hint_md: Use $h_K\geq r$ to turn an additive support error into a multiplicative one.

sources.locator: Exercise 2.2, p. 61; volume counterexamples in §2.2.3.2, p. 37; convex specialization; English edition (2018), printed pages

problems.title: For convex bodies, boundary distance equals body distance
problems.statement_md:
For compact convex bodies $K,L\subset\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interior, prove
$$d_H(\partial K,\partial L)=d_H(K,L).$$
You may use the signed-distance formula from support functions. Explain why the result fails for general compact sets, using the grids $G_n\subset[0,1]$.
problems.hint_md: Bound signed-distance differences by support-function differences. For the reverse inequality, take convex hulls of the boundaries.

problems.title: Diameter and enclosing radius are Lipschitz stable
problems.statement_md:
For nonempty compact $K,L$, prove
$$|\operatorname{diam}K-\operatorname{diam}L|\leq2d_H(K,L),\qquad |R(K)-R(L)|\leq d_H(K,L),$$
where $R$ is the smallest enclosing-ball radius. If $K,L$ are convex bodies, prove also $|r(K)-r(L)|\leq d_H(K,L)$ for the inradius. Show the constants are sharp using concentric balls.
problems.hint_md: Approximate a pair of diameter endpoints, enlarge an enclosing ball, and use the support characterization of a contained ball.

sources.locator: Exercise 2.2, p. 61; compact-set topology in §2.2.3.2; radius companions; English edition (2018), printed pages

problems.title: Why intersection is not pointwise minimum
problems.statement_md: Let $K,L$ be nonempty compact convex sets with $K\cap L\ne\varnothing$. Show that $h_{K\cap L}\leq\min(h_K,h_L)$, and give intersecting planar disks for which the inequality is strict in some direction.
problems.hint_md: Try two unit disks with centers $(\pm a,0)$, where $0<a<1$, and compare their highest points with the highest point of their lens.

problems.title: Constant width through the difference body
problems.statement_md: Prove that a compact convex body $K$ has constant width $w>0$ if and only if $K+(-K)=wB$, where $B$ is the unit ball. Deduce that positive Minkowski combinations of constant-width bodies have width equal to the same combination of their widths.
problems.hint_md: Compute the support function of $-K$ first. The support of the difference body records the width in each direction.

problems.title: Diameter, strict convexity, and opposite contact points
problems.statement_md: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body of constant width $w>0$. Show that its diameter is $w$, each supporting hyperplane meets $K$ at just one point, and the two opposite contact points differ by $wu$ in normal direction $u$.
problems.hint_md: Project any chord onto its own direction. For opposite contact points, compare the length of the chord with the length of its projection onto the support normal.

problems.title: The only centrally symmetric constant-width body
problems.statement_md: Prove that a centrally symmetric constant-width body of width $w$ is a ball of radius $w/2$.
problems.hint_md: Translate the center of symmetry to the origin. What does symmetry do to $h_K(u)$ and $h_K(-u)$?

sources.locator: §7, Exercise 7-7, printed p. 74

problems.title: Constant width survives orthogonal projection
problems.statement_md: Let $E$ be a linear subspace of positive dimension; widths of subsets of $E$ are measured within $E$. Prove that the orthogonal projection of a body of width $w$ onto $E$ has width $w$. Deduce that every planar shadow of a three-dimensional constant-width body has perimeter $\pi w$, using Barbier’s theorem.
problems.hint_md: For a unit vector $u$ in the projection plane, compare $x\cdot u$ with $(\operatorname{proj}_E x)\cdot u$.

problems.title: Concentric incircle and circumcircle
problems.statement_md: For a constant-width body $K$ of width $w$, prove that an inball and a smallest enclosing ball can be chosen with the same center and that $r(K)+R(K)=w$.
problems.hint_md: For a proposed center $c$, look at the maximum and minimum of $h_K(u)-c\cdot u$. The constant-width identity relates these two extrema.

problems.title: A constant-width body is an intersection of balls
problems.statement_md: Prove $K=\bigcap_{x\in K}B(x,w)$ for a body of width $w$. Deduce spindle convexity: the intersection of all radius-$w$ balls containing two points of $K$ lies in $K$.
problems.hint_md: The diameter bound proves one inclusion. To exclude a point outside $K$, separate it by a support plane and use the opposite contact point as a ball center.

problems.title: Boundary, curvature, perimeter, and area from support
problems.statement_md: Suppose $h$ is a $C^2$, $2\pi$-periodic planar support function with $\rho=h+h''>0$. Put $n=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ and $t=(-\sin\theta,\cos\theta)$. Derive $X=hn+h't$, $X'=\rho t$, $P=\int_0^{2\pi}h$, and $A=\frac12\int_0^{2\pi}(h^2-h'^2)$.
problems.hint_md: Differentiate $X(\theta)\cdot n(\theta)=h(\theta)$, remembering that $X\prime$ is tangent to the curve. Use Green’s formula for the area.

problems.title: Barbier’s theorem from projected variation
problems.statement_md: Prove that a planar convex body of constant width $w$ has perimeter $\pi w$. You may approximate convex bodies by convex polygons, with perimeter continuous under Hausdorff convergence.
problems.hint_md: First work with a convex polygon. Its boundary projection onto a line travels from the minimum to the maximum and back. Integrate this total variation over directions.

problems.title: A smooth noncircular family of constant-width curves
problems.statement_md: Fix $w>0$. For an odd integer $m\geq3$, consider $h(\theta)=w/2+a\cos(m\theta)$. Find the exact range of $a$ for which $h$ is a support function, and compute its area. Explain why this gives uncountably many noncircular examples with reflection symmetry.
problems.hint_md: Check the antipodal sum and the sign of $h+h\prime\prime$ separately. Orthogonality of Fourier modes simplifies the area integral.

problems.title: The 120-degree corner bound
problems.statement_md: Let a planar convex body have constant width $w>0$. Show that any corner has interior angle at least $120^\circ$. If equality occurs, prove that the body is a Reuleaux triangle.
problems.hint_md: The normal directions at a corner produce an opposite circular arc. Apply the diameter bound to the two endpoints of that arc.

problems.title: Pál’s theorem: a circumscribed regular hexagon
problems.statement_md: Prove Pál's theorem: every planar body of constant width $w$ admits a circumscribed regular hexagon whose opposite sides are distance $w$ apart. In particular, every unit constant-width body admits such a hexagon with opposite-side separation one. Compute its side length and area. The hexagon itself is not a body of constant width: here “width $w$” means its minimum width (the distance between opposite sides).
problems.hint_md: Write $h=w/2+g$ with $g(\theta+\pi)=-g(\theta)$. Look for an orientation where the sum of $g$ at three normals separated by $2\pi/3$ vanishes.

problems.title: Two similar copies cannot have greater total perimeter
problems.statement_md: Let $K$ be a planar constant-width body, and let $K_1,K_2\subset K$ be similar copies of $K$ with positive similarity ratios and disjoint interiors. Prove $P(K_1)+P(K_2)\leq P(K)$. Rotations of the copies are allowed.
problems.hint_md: Separate the interiors of the two copies by a line. Compare their widths in its normal direction with the width of the container.

problems.title: Existence of a least-volume constant-width body
problems.statement_md: Fix $d\geq2$ and $w>0$. Prove that volume attains its minimum among width-$w$ convex bodies. You may use Hausdorff compactness of nonempty compact subsets of a fixed compact set, stability of convexity, and continuity of volume for convex bodies.
problems.hint_md: Translate each candidate to contain the origin. The diameter bound gives a common containing ball; pass constant width to the Hausdorff limit through the support functions.

problems.title: An enclosing ball forces a concentric ball inside
problems.statement_md:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body of constant width $w>0$ and suppose $K\subset B(c,R)$ with $0\leq R\leq w$. Prove
$$B(c,w-R)\subset K.$$
In particular, a width-$w$ body inside a radius-$w$ ball contains the center. Show that two width-$w$ bodies with disjoint interiors cannot both fit in a ball of radius strictly less than $w$.
problems.hint_md: Translate $c$ to zero. An upper bound on one support value gives a lower bound on its opposite.

problems.title: Farthest distance and signed distance to the body
problems.statement_md:
For a width-$w$ convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, set $F(c)=\max_{x\in K}|x-c|$. Prove
$$F(c)=\begin{cases}w+\operatorname{dist}(c,K),&c\notin K,\\w-\operatorname{dist}(c,\partial K),&c\in K.\end{cases}$$
Deduce $F(c)=w$ exactly on $\partial K$.
problems.hint_md: Express the farthest distance as the maximum of translated support values, then replace $u$ by $-u$.

problems.title: Where may the center of a covering ball move?
problems.statement_md:
For a fixed width-$w$ body $K$, let $E_R(K)=\{c:K\subset B(c,R)\}$ be the set of centers of radius-$R$ covering balls. Prove
$$E_R(K)=\begin{cases}K\ominus(w-R)B,&0\leq R\leq w,\\K+(R-w)B,&R\geq w,\end{cases}$$
where $K\ominus tB=\{c:c+tB\subset K\}$. Thus $E_w(K)=K$. The eroded set may be empty.
problems.hint_md: Write containment in support form and use the constant-width identity to solve the inequalities for the center.
